# Data-quality notes (generated by scripts/01_eda.py)

- Trips: train 80, student_test 10. Missing values in .track files: 0. Invalid coordinates removed: 0. Duplicate timestamps removed: 0. Out-of-order timestamps: 0.
- Sampling is nominally 1 Hz: 96.7% of steps are exactly 1 s. 30 trips contain at least one gap over 30 s (longest 153064 s).
- Each trip ships its own road-network extract (median 9305 nodes, 18762 arcs). Trips are spread across many countries, so a per-trip local projection is used.
- Reference routes are continuous chains of arcs (minimum continuity 0.981). They list arcs, not GPS points, so a monotone alignment (pathsnap/labeling.py) assigns each GPS point a reference arc.
- Trips whose median GPS-to-reference distance is over 50 m: 00000033, 00000054 (see plots/eda_trajectory_00000033.png: the reference route covers only part of the drive, so GPS points on the uncovered part are aligned to a distant arc).
- The longest single time gap is 153064 s; such gaps are kept and the HMM widens its transition model with the gap length.
- Decision: training rows from GPS points more than 60 m from their aligned reference arc are dropped as unreliable labels (10.7% of training points). Evaluation tables report accuracy on all points.
